name: Pippit
summary: AI marketing-content maker by CapCut — turns a product link into marketing videos, avatar presenters, talking photos and sales posters, with scheduling and multi-platform publishing. Credit-based, with a free tier that needs no card. Seedance 2.5 is now listed among its video models: clips up to 30 seconds, text timestamps to pin key moments, footage extension for longer scenes and reference inputs to steer the direction — although their own model page still describes it with "upcoming" wording (checked 4 Aug 2026). A separate Story Studio section has since appeared in their own navigation, grouping AI Drama, AI film, AI Movie, AI Script and AI Workflow (checked 3 Sep 2026).
best_for: solo founders and small teams that want a steady stream of product-marketing videos and posters generated from a product link, without filming anything
skip_if: you need dependable output on a deadline — buyer reviews describe failed generations that still consume credits, and support that answers in weeks rather than days
honest_knock: The meter is credits per attempt, not per usable result — and buyer reviews centre on exactly that. Trustpilot reviewers describe generations that failed but still consumed their credits, refunds that were hard to get, and support replies measured in weeks. A tool that charges for its own failures puts the cost of unreliability on you.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per year on the yearly tab (list price EUR 145)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-19 on pippit.ai/pricing from a Netherlands exit; the page prices in the visitor's currency, so these are euro amounts) Every tier was repriced and every credit allowance cut since our 6 September reading, so treat any older figure, ours included, as withdrawn. The page opens on the Yearly tab. Yearly: Free €0 with recurring daily credits and no card; Starter €87 a year against a struck-through €145; Plus €213 against €355; Pro is a five-step ladder at €467, €948, €1,260, €1,901 and €3,117 against list prices of €779, €1,580, €2,100, €3,169 and €5,195, with the €1,901 step shown by default. Monthly: Starter €8 (list €13), Plus €19 (list €31), and the same five Pro steps at €41, €83, €110, €166 and €270 against lists of €68, €137.99, €184, €277 and €450. Every card is marked 38% to 40% off. The allowances that go with them, identical on both billing tabs: 1,575 credits a month on Starter, 3,885 on Plus, and 8,645 / 17,600 / 23,500 / 35,500 / 59,000 across the five Pro steps, with 1, 3 and 10 seats respectively. Two things changed shape rather than level. Pro gained a new bottom step at 8,645 credits, so the ladder is five prices where it was four. And the credits-per-euro ratio the page prints beside each card — EUR1=217.24, 218.87 and 224.09 — is now arithmetically correct for yearly billing; on 6 September the same line was a hundredfold off its own figures. All amounts here were taken from the page's own SKU payload, which carries the charged amount, the list price, the discount percentage, the credit quota and the seat count for every plan on both tabs.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the free plan, with an existing account Daan had made on 14 August 2026; our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We asked the agent for one simple image and downloaded it.
findings: The credit history showed 400 trial credits from August that expired after 30 days, and 40 free credits that were valid for one day only.
With 0 credits the first request opened the subscription screen. The day's 40 free credits appeared a few minutes after logging in.
The agent made the image in about 25 seconds for 2 credits. It spelled our test text exactly.
The download was a 2048 × 2048 JPEG, though the canvas called it a .png. It carried a 'Pippit AI' watermark in the corner.
Starter was €13 a month for 1,575 credits, or €145 a year; the plan screen opened on yearly billing.
not_tested: A brand-new account and its trial
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
